entries.title: Sixth beluga whale rescued from Canada dies in San Diego, following four deaths at the Shedd
entries.summary: <p>Another beluga whale rescued from the shuttered Marineland aquarium in Ontario, Canada, has died, SeaWorld in San Diego announced.</p><p>Cyprus, a 9-year-old beluga, stopped eating this weekend and declined quickly, said a Facebook post from the aquarium. He was initially doing well since arriving in San Diego in August, but belugas, like many species, can hide their discomfort or face underlying health concerns, the facility said.</p><p>That brings the total number of Marineland whales to die since being rescued to six, including four at Chicago's Shedd Aquarium and one at Oceanografic Valencia in Spain.</p><p>At the Shedd, the most recent death was Caspian, a 27-year-old female, that died Oct. 7. Peekachu, a 23-year-old female, died Aug. 25, and Rain, a 20-year-old female, died Sept. 2. Osiris, a 26-year-old female, died Sept. 21. The rescued beluga in Spain, Jelly Bean, died Sept. 18.</p><p>A resident beluga at the Shedd, Beethoven, also died recently at 34, likely due to age-related issues, the aquarium said.</p><p>Marineland closed this summer after facing financial ruin and loud criticism from animal rights activists, some of whom have also questioned the safety of transferring the whales to other aquariums.</p><p>The SeaWorld post said, "Like our colleagues at the other AZA-accredited facilities that rescued these belugas, we understood each animal would be navigating a significant transition and that their complete health picture, including conditions that may have developed over time, could only become clearer through ongoing assessment and care."</p><p>SeaWorld is still working to acclimate the rest of the belugas from Marineland, and staff acknowledged it would take time for the animals to adjust.</p><p>"The other rescued belugas in our care continue to be in stable health and remain under close monitoring as they continue to adjust to their surroundings," the aquarium said. "As we have indicated, this process will take a considerable amount of time. Our commitment to the health, well-being and care of these belugas, like every animal we rescue, continues." </p>

entries.title: Analyzing Game 1 of the WNBA Finals
entries.summary: <p>SAN FRANCISCO — You’re probably feeling pretty annoyed right now if you’re the Dream, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/wnba/2026/10/17/valkyries-fans-meet-coach-natalie-nakases-expectations-in-game-1-of-the-wnba-finals" >having lost a Game 1</a> in which you led for 75% of it, and had the Valkyries offense looking like a fish flopping on land.</p><p>In fact, the half-court offense appeared so halting and uncertain about where any openings were that I had to ask a couple of Bay Area journalists after the game what the Valkyries’ strategy on offense even is.</p><p>They said it was waiting for the Dream to make a mistake.</p><p>The problem with that is that the Dream don’t make very many. They’re long, quick, and in each other’s gaps. As a result, so many Valkyries possessions ended in a desperation heave, or a forced drive into Dream defenders that hadn’t been shifted.</p><p>The Dream enjoyed a lead for much of the third quarter until a Valkyries run — which included a Kiah Stokes tip-in, an unlikely roll on a Kaila Charles’ three-point shot, and a breakdown from the Dream leaving Charles wide open for a layup — gave them the lead.</p><p>Even through his normal stoicism, you could tell Dream coach Karl Smesko was very attuned to how luck and tiny mistakes swung the game in the Valkyries favor.</p><p>“I thought our team defended excellent, but when a game is this close even a couple breakdowns can make the difference,” Smesko said.</p><p>The problem that Smesko likely spent Sunday mulling over is that the Dream’s half-court offense was really no better than the Valkyries’. Though I’m no expert on the the Dream either, I can tell you that the one thing every half-court offense is supposed to do — swing the ball from one side of the court to the other — did not happen. Like the Valkyries, it was a lot of one pass then fire away.</p><p>“We had a couple of dry spells where we just weren’t working together as well as you need to against this [Valkyries] defense,” Smesko said.</p><p>They also turned their back on what had been working from the jump. Forward Angel Reese built them a lead in the first quarter, then only touched the ball in scoring position twice in the second half.</p><p>“Maybe that was just on me,” Reese said. “I wasn’t aggressive enough with the ball and trying to get the ball and to get to spots.<br>So definitely going to do a better job of that next game.”</p><p>Smesko also took responsibility, saying they need to do a better job getting the ball to Reese.</p><p>The bright side is that “giving Reese the ball” and actually moving the ball from side to side don’t really seem that difficult to correct heading into Game 2. The other bright side is that despite Dream superstar Rhyne Howard finishing with a measly 12 points, they still only lost by four. They also had two wide-open shots at the end that could have won the game.</p><p>“Naz [Hillmon] had a good look at three,” Smesko said. “Rhyne had a good look at three. We knock down either of those we’re not talking about whatever mistakes we made.</p><p>“But that’s what this game comes down to. You have two shots go in and out. At some point in the game, they bank in a three. We were right there. So that’s why it hurts a little bit. But it also motivates us. We know we’re capable of doing.”</p><p>This WNBA Finals represents a changing of the guard. The Valkyries and Dream knocked off the Aces and the Liberty, super-teams that have dominated the last five years, and they reached the pinnacle in large part by feasting on other teams’ mistakes.</p><p>Which is why Game 1 felt like such a staring contest; there just aren’t very many mistakes left to be mined.</p>

entries.title: Evanston, New Trier investigate reports of racist, homophobic slurs during football game at new Ryan Field
entries.summary: <p>Two suburban school districts are investigating after reports of homophobic and racist slurs at Friday night's football game between the two schools. Played at Northwestern University's newly opened Ryan Field, the game was supposed to be a season highlight for New Trier and Evanston Township high schools. More than 25,000 fans attended, according to some reports.</p><p>New Trier fans directed racist and homophobic comments toward members of the Evanston marching band, according to a joint statement from both districts' superintendents.</p><p>"Friday evening should have been an opportunity to celebrate our students, spirited competition, and the longstanding traditions of our two school communities," the statement said. "For the ETHS Marching Band, it was an especially meaningful opportunity to do what they love: share their talents and proudly represent their school. No student should leave an event where they came to perform, compete, or support their peers feeling that their dignity or belonging were demeaned."</p><p>Administrators at both districts are working together to investigate the reports and encourage anyone with information about the incident to contact their school's administration.</p>

entries.title: Bears beat Falcons 31-23 in QB Caleb Williams' return
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback Caleb Williams stepped up in the pocket, shuffled right and started sprinting toward the sideline. He looked downfield until he locked eyes with his biggest target, then threw across his body toward tight end Colston Loveland, who was sandwiched between two Falcons defenders at the goal line.</p><p>Loveland caught the ball as he was smacked by the two players for the first touchdown of the Bears’ 31-23 victory Sunday against the Falcons. Williams soon delivered another hit — a gentle head bump — before taking off his helmet and celebrating on the sideline.</p><p>‘‘Just let it rip,’’ Williams said. ‘‘Let the emotions rip.’’</p><p>It was a show of emotion a month in the making, ever since Williams suffered a torn right hamstring in the fourth quarter of a Week 2 loss against the Vikings. And it was a spark the Bears desperately needed in the wake of a 31-7 thrashing at the hands of the Packers a week ago.</p><p>Williams’ performance was much more than a ball of emotion, however. He was a stone-cold assassin, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a 111.2 passer rating. He completed his first 12 passes, including a third-down hook-and-ladder to wide receiver Rome Odunze, who shoveled the ball to running back Roschon Johnson. It set up the touchdown to Loveland, who finished with a season-high 65 yards on six catches.</p><p>In a clean pocket, Williams went 24-for-24 for 248 yards, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. No NFL quarterback has completed that many passes without an incompletion since at least 2018.</p><p>‘‘Let the emotions fly,’’ Williams said. ‘‘But when it’s time to be in control, when it’s time to lock in and look the guys in the eyes, they want to feel your control over yourself, your control of the huddle. And then from there we can go out there and execute.’’</p><p>It was one of the best performances of Williams’ career. Given the stakes, it might have been the most important. The Bears were at a ‘‘crossroads,’’ coach Ben Johnson said, after losing to the Packers. Williams reset their direction. His teammates felt it.</p><p>‘‘He has the juice,’’ Odunze said.</p><p>As an added bonus, Williams said his hamstring wasn’t sore after the game, though he’ll need to continue treatment for it through the rest of the season. Williams ran four times for three yards, including a two-yard sneak for a first down with 2:46 lefty. That was far different than his last complete game, when he ran 10 times for 65 yards in Week 1.</p><p>This was the dream scenario the Bears had in mind when they decided to start Williams a week after Tyson Bagent struggled against the Packers. The plan started with a brief meeting in Johnson’s office early last week.</p><p>‘‘I walked in his office, dapped him up and said, ‘Let’s get this going this week,’ ’’ Williams said. ‘‘And I walked out after that.’’</p><p>The energy from Williams’ return crackled through the stadium. The Bears led 14-0 at the end of the first quarter and never trailed. There were so many Bears fans inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium that the Falcons practiced all week with crowd noise and used a silent count on offense. The crowd erupted with every Williams success.</p><p>The Bears’ defense felt the energy, too, giving up seven points through the first three quarters. The Falcons rallied for 16 points in the fourth and marched for a touchdown against Bears backups before Johnson put the starters back in. The Bears were trying to lighten the defensive workload with a game Thursday against the Patriots, Johnson said, but reversed course to lock down the victory.</p><p>The Bears’ special-teamers got in on the act, too, recovering a fumbled kickoff and a muffed punt — the latter on Tory Taylor’s curving ‘‘banana ball’’ — that contributed to 10 points.</p><p>‘‘The fact that we started fast, really in all three phases, was huge for us, as well as something that we had also talked about the night before,’’ Johnson said. ‘‘If you could write a script, that’s what we would want to do against a team like this. We’ve got to come out of the gate hot.’’</p><p>Earlier in the week, it was Williams who was hot. He used his first news conference since Sept. 23 to rail against what he said were erroneous reports about the severity of his injury. What went unspoken was his<br>annoyance with those who mocked him leaving the game against the Vikings emotional and on a golf cart.</p><p>Williams made no mention of that beef after the game. But as he jogged to the locker room after the victory, he looked at the assembled media and, with a smile, paraphrased an old Kirk Cousins line.</p><p>‘‘Y’all like that?’’ he said.</p><p>The answer from the teammates waiting for him in the locker room — and from fans at home and in the stadium — was a resounding yes.</p><p>When Williams entered the locker room, he got a game ball. He told his teammates how hard it was to fight through the injury.</p><p>‘‘It was just me having a consistent positive mindset throughout the weeks over myself — and about myself — of being able to get back, trying to get back, fighting to get back,’’ Williams said. ‘‘And when I get back, just to show them who I am. And who we are.’’</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-falcons-grades-caleb-williams-kyler-gordon-colston-loveland-chicago-atlanta-nfl" >Bears’ grades are in. How did they do against the Falcons?</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-ben-johnson-was-back-in-his-bag-in-crossroads-win-against-falcons" >Bears’ Ben Johnson was back in his bag in ‘crossroads’ win against Falcons</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-cb-kyler-gordon-goes-off-with-3-sacks-in-return-from-injury-everything-i-wanted" >Bears CB Kyler Gordon gets 3 sacks in return from injury in 31-23 win vs. Falcons: ‘Everything I wanted’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: City Colleges of Chicago reach late-night tentative contract agreement to avoid strike
entries.summary: <p>The Cook County College Teachers Union, Local 1600, and the City Colleges of Chicago reached an overnight tentative contract agreement just hours before a strike was set to kick off Monday. </p><p>The contract is for four years and includes salaries that keep pace with inflation, protected health insurance, safeguards toward AI and a path toward free developmental education, according to a press release from the union. </p><p>"I am proud of our negotiating teams, of our members who were prepared to strike, and of this contract,” said CCCTU President Tony Johnston. “It should not have taken until 3:45 a.m. the day of a strike to get here. But we are happy to reach a fair agreement that supports students, faculty, and professionals.”</p><p>The agreement must now go to the membership for a ratification vote. If members approve, the agreement will go to the City Colleges Board of Trustees for approval.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Family holiday gatherings feel lonely for single guy
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I'm a single male who's happy with his life, with plenty of friends and family. My issue is what I endure during the holidays. Every year, I'm invited over to Thanksgiving and Christmas, and I look forward to seeing family that I only see once or twice a year.</p><p>These get-togethers usually consist of 15 to 25 people. Yet, other than having the chance to say hello and goodbye, everyone breaks into cliques while I sit there the whole time with no one ever showing any interest in engaging in conversation with me. I've reached the point where this isolation has me feeling depressed and lonely even though I'm surrounded by people.</p><p>I've come to realize I'd be happier spending the holidays by myself. Would it be wrong to start declining these invitations and politely explain why? I mentioned this to family members in the past, and they've acknowledged the issue, but it continues to happen every time. — <i>INVISIBLE IN THE CROWD</i></p><p><b>DEAR INVISIBLE:</b> You are in charge of your own destiny. You don't have to sit on the sofa watching the rest of the guests socialize with each other. You could get up, walk over to the various groups and attempt to join the conversation. You could also go to these gatherings for a short time to wish your relatives a Happy Thanksgiving, Merry Christmas, Happy New Year, etc., and then leave to do something with friends or return home. As to explaining your absence to your hosts, it's not necessary to state your reason for skipping the event.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My maid of honor and I aren't seeing eye to eye on my bridal shower. I was clear about not wanting a surprise shower and about my wish to be kept informed about the preparation. She had decided to plan a surprise shower with a guest list of only 20 people. When she found out I wanted one with about 40 people (I have a large family and a moderate number of close friends), she got upset. She said I shouldn't be involved at all in the planning and that it's not proper etiquette.</p><p>Knowing her financial situation, I offered to cover the expenses and participate in the planning process. However, she isn't willing to accept my help. She believes that this isn't the way it should be and said she won't be able to plan it the way I want. She has now decided to forgo any role in planning it. Who is in the wrong here? — <i>ALMOST-BRIDE IN THE EAST</i></p><p><b>DEAR ALMOST-BRIDE:</b> She is. Because she's unwilling to coordinate with you and isn't comfortable with you paying for the shower she's unable to afford, she has done you a favor by speaking up now. (She has also indicated that maybe she's not maid of honor material.) Since you want a much larger shower than she was willing to provide, perhaps another friend or relative of yours will be willing to step in and help you plan the shower you were hoping for.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: A new Chicago brewery is creating Korea’s oldest alcoholic drink
entries.summary: <p>Korea’s oldest alcoholic drink is now being brewed in Chicago.</p><p>Yido on the Near West Side specializes in brewing makgeolli, an unfiltered rice wine that’s naturally fermented with a starter culture — similar to kombucha. The drink is often described as being creamy, tart and sweet with fruity notes.</p><p>“I feel like Chicago is a city that's like a food and drink city,” Yido Brews founder Peter Quinn Woo Chung said. “It really cares about local craft and artisan creators, and so it just seemed like a big unfilled gap.”</p><p>Makgeolli has slowly <a class="Link" href="https://www.saveur.com/food/hana-makgeolli-alice-jun-spreading-korean-alcohol-and-culture/" target="_blank" ><u>grown in popularity</u></a> <a class="Link" href="https://www.forbes.com/sites/annakang/2020/05/15/korean-makgeolli-the-next-alcohol-trend-to-watch/?sh=7d04309b6740" target="_blank" ><u>in the U.S.</u></a> In South Korea, there are over <a class="Link" href="https://www.saveur.com/food/hana-makgeolli-alice-jun-spreading-korean-alcohol-and-culture/" target="_blank" ><u>760 licensed breweries</u></a> that produce over 2,000 varieties of the drink. In 2020, Hana Makgeolli opened in New York City – and it was known as the <a class="Link" href="https://www.mashed.com/1176649/new-york-city-is-home-to-the-only-makgeolli-brewery-in-the-us/" target="_blank" ><u>only commercial makgeolli brewery in U.S</u></a>. at the time. Since then, a handful more have opened across the country, including in <a class="Link" href="https://www.instagram.com/sangmakgeolli/?hl=en" target="_blank" ><u>California</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://jsbrewery.com/" target="_blank" ><u>Maryland</u></a> and <a class="Link" href="https://rainbrew.com/" target="_blank" ><u>Washington</u></a>.</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: Almost all lawsuits brought in Chicago's federal court over deadly Boeing 737 MAX crashes have been resolved
entries.summary: <p>Sales of Boeing Co.’s 737 MAX jetliners are soaring, with orders of the aircraft reaching record levels this year.</p><p>Boeing is also nearing a darker milestone. It’s resolved almost all litigation brought by families of the nearly 350 people killed in two overseas 737 MAX crashes, with a jury awarding the survivors of one of those who perished, Michael “Mick” Ryan, $29 million in August in Chicago’s federal courthouse.</p><p>Earlier in the year, a Chicago jury awarded the survivors of Samya Stumo nearly $50 million.</p><p>And last fall, a Chicago jury awarded about $28 million to the family of another crash victim, Shikha Garg.</p><p>Because Boeing was based in Chicago until its headquarters moved to Arlington, Virginia, in recent years, hundreds of lawsuits were centered at the Dirksen Federal Building in the South Loop.</p><p>While there were several high-profile verdicts within the last year, the vast majority of the cases were settled before they could go to trial and with confidentiality clauses.</p><p>Accordingly, plaintiff lawyers and Boeing officials won’t say how much has been paid out so far in total, though it’s likely in the billions of dollars.</p><p>And that doesn’t include costs and penalties associated with other legal problems that followed the 737 MAX crashes, including a now-concluded U.S. Justice Department investigation.</p><p>One 737 MAX crashed in 2018 shortly after taking off from an Indonesian airport, killing all 189 people aboard. In 2019, another 737 MAX went down in Ethiopia, killing all 157 on board.</p><p>Boeing initially tried blaming the pilots. But a flawed system that can affect flight controls — a system Boeing wasn’t truthful about with federal regulators, the airlines or the public — turned out to be a factor in both crashes.</p><p>The model was temporarily grounded while problems were fixed.</p><p>Boeing’s image has taken a beating ever since, and other problems have emerged, including in 2024 when a door plug on a 737 MAX blew out after departing Portland, Oregon.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-b10000" represented 72 of the families who lost loved ones in the Ethiopia crash and was appointed lead counsel for 163 lawsuits stemming from that disaster.</p><p>“Of those 163 lawsuits, only two remain pending,” a representative of the law firm said. “Clifford Law Offices does not represent the plaintiffs in either of those remaining cases. All others have resolved, either by settlement or verdict, or have been dismissed voluntarily.</p><p>“All settlement terms are confidential, per the releases signed by the clients.”</p><p>At least 89 other lawsuits were brought in Chicago by families of those killed in the Indonesia crash, and they also have been resolved, according to people familiar with those cases.</p><p>Miami-area attorney Steven C. Marks handled around 40 of those Indonesia suits, all of which he said ended in settlements. He's representing the plaintiff in one of the two pending cases.</p><p>He also represented Ryan’s widow, Naoise Connolly Ryan, in the recent verdict involving her late husband who was killed in the Ethiopia crash.</p><p>Michael Ryan was chief engineer for the United Nations World Food Programme, and the agency’s web site said the father of two, who was from Ireland, “worked in reconstruction and rehabilitation but also capacity building — showing communities how to help themselves.”</p><p>“During the 2014-16 Ebola outbreak in Liberia, Mick built medical centres to treat those with the virus and prevent others from being infected. To achieve this, he had construction sites operating at all hours for six weeks.”</p><p>In Bangladesh, according to the UN, “Mick not only organized the building of shelters and infrastructure, he also supported the stabilization of the ground and planned evacuations, which saved tens of thousands of Rohingya refugees from the threat of landslides and floods.”</p><p>Stumo, a 24-year-old nonprofit worker, and Garg, a 36-year-old UN consultant, also perished in the Ethiopia crash.</p><p>Boeing released a statement saying: “We are deeply sorry to all who lost loved ones on Lion Air Flight 610 and Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302. While we have resolved nearly all of these claims through settlements, families are entitled to pursue their claims through the court process, and we respect their right to do so.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2024/08/27/boeing-campaign-contributions-illinois-don-harmon-emanuel-chris-welch" target="_blank" >Top Illinois political figures still like Boeing’s campaign money despite its troubles</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/08/31/boeing-chicago-campaign-contributions-illinois-congressional-delegation-northwest-indiana-michael-quigley" target="_blank" >Boeing’s image is deeply bruised, but the company’s campaign money is still good with Illinois politicians</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Gov. JB Pritzker signals more optimism on Bears stadium deal — maybe even in Chicago — as election nears
entries.summary: <p>Landing a stadium deal for a professional sports team is a delicate proposition for any elected official.</p><p>Nobody wants to give the farm away to a multibillion-dollar franchise like the Chicago Bears, but the alternative is just as bad — especially in a football-crazed state like Illinois.</p><p>“I’m just glad I’m not going to be known as the governor that lost the Bears,” Republican gubernatorial nominee Darren Bailey said in <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/13/watch-illinois-gov-debate-jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-takeaways" target="_blank" ><u>a debate last week</u></a> with Gov. JB Pritzker, seemingly resigned to the team’s Indiana defection.</p><p>But as the Nov. 3 election nears, Pritzker has indicated he’s increasingly confident he and other Democratic leaders in Springfield can get the best of both worlds while carrying a stadium deal across the goal line.</p><p>The incumbent’s optimism seems to be cresting for a resolution arriving five years after the Bears’ drive for a new home began, 11 months after the team’s first Hoosier threat — and a few weeks after the polls close.</p><p>And it could even happen in Chicago, Pritzker says, which had been all but eliminated from the Bears’ conversation for the past year in favor of Arlington Heights.</p><p>“I believe that in November, we’re going to be able to get something done to keep the Bears in the state of Illinois,” Pritzker said. “But I’m not going to do it at the expense of the taxpayers.”</p><p>Convenient timing, if you ask Bailey, who’s trying to win over voters himself in his second bid to unseat Pritzker. Lawmakers return to Springfield two weeks after the Nov. 3 election.</p><p>But the GOP challenger’s proposal to keep the Bears in their home state sounds remarkably similar to ones Pritzker has supported over his tenure. The same goes for independent gubernatorial candidate Collin Corbett, who agrees it should be a priority.</p><p>“If you're ever going to turn around the reputation of a state like Illinois, the Bears are one business, but they're a very public and a very loud business,” Corbett said. “We need to show that we're open for business, that we want to grow, and no, that doesn't mean you're going to get a big, sweetheart deal.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-810000" class="Figure-credit"><p>Provided by Manica Architecture</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3><b>Another tone shift in stadium talks</b></h3><p>Pritzker has rejected the prospect of any giveaways for the Bears since the McCaskeys entered a deal to acquire the old Arlington International Racecourse property in 2021.</p><p>But <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/01/16/chicago-bears-stadium-northwest-indiana-arlington-heights-jb-pritzker-kam-buckner" target="_blank" ><u>the governor’s tone changed considerably</u></a> after the team’s threat last fall to move to Indiana, following years of Chicago legislators rolling their eyes at overtures for a bill affording the Bears long-term property tax breaks on the 326-acre northwest suburban site.</p><p>Pritzker backed off previous suggestions the Bears should pay off lingering debt from Soldier Field’s 2003 renovation and began emphasizing his support for public funding of potentially hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of infrastructure upgrades around a potential dome.</p><p>Most importantly, Pritzker took on a more active role in stadium negotiations than the passive presence from his office that lobbyists and some legislators close to the discussions had privately grumbled about for years.</p><p>The governor is driving the talks now, meeting again earlier this month with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, whose repeated visits to Illinois might suggest the league’s not thrilled at the prospect of breaking ground on a Hammond dome.</p><p>Pritzker has supported the broader concept of allowing the Bears to negotiate a discounted payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) with local governments. The Illinois House passed such a bill this spring, earning critical support from Chicago Democrats because it would’ve shared proceeds with homeowners as property tax rebates — but those returns were deemed “<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/05/04/bears-stadium-property-tax-relief-pritzker-negligible" target="_blank" ><u>negligible</u></a>.”</p><p>The Illinois Senate passed a separate bill that would allow municipalities to create their own stadium authorities to negotiate terms of a publicly owned stadium, but it crumbled in the waning hours of spring session <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears-stadium/2026/05/31/bears-stadium-bill-springfield-arlington-heights-hammond-indiana" target="_blank" ><u>without a vote in the other chamber</u></a>.</p><p>Sources familiar with the negotiations say the conversation has shifted toward the stadium authority model. That would mean no tax bill for the Bears — and it'd keep the door open to Chicago, providing vital cover for city legislators loath to pave the team's path to Arlington Heights.</p><p>While there hasn’t been a clear breakthrough, optimism is growing for a bill to move by January’s lame-duck session, if not this fall’s veto session. Pritzker raised the stakes by taking the under on that timeline.</p><p>“The legislation that is being discussed now would give the option for the possibility that there would be a stadium built in the city or in Arlington Heights,” Pritzker said last week. “We want to keep them in the state of Illinois. If we give them those two options, I think that would be satisfactory.</p><p>“In the end, this is up to the Bears,” he added.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-100000" name="image-100000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/618c9c1/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ff35a8a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a307320/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Republican nominee Darren Bailey laughs beside Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker before the start of the televised WTTW News Gubernatorial Forum on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a307320/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/3c93549/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/a307320/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fdd%2F99%2Fa55ca32b4ba98cae3aecdbe43a21%2Fgovdebate-261015-14.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Republican nominee Darren Bailey laughs beside Democratic Gov. JB Pritzker before the start of the televised WTTW News Gubernatorial Forum on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Victor Hilitski/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3><b>A familiar Bears stadium pitch from Darren Bailey</b></h3><p>Bailey, taking <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/13/jb-pritzker-darren-bailey-collin-corbett-illinois-governor-election-november-midterm" >another shot at the gubernatorial end zone</a> four years after losing to Pritzker, suggested a Bears move to Indiana is a fait accompli based on his own conversations with Indiana Gov. Mike Braun. Hoosier lawmakers rolled out the red carpet in February with a generous legislative package that would put $1 billion into a Bears dome.</p><p>But last month, Bailey wore a Bears jersey while offering up his own so-called “I-Formation Plan” to entice the team to stay in-state.</p><p>The crux of the downstate proposal is a PILOT incentive similar to what Pritzker has supported, which passed the Illinois House but was dead on arrival amid stiff opposition from Chicago Democrats in the state Senate.</p><p>“Rejecting a bad deal does not excuse JB Pritzker from finding a better one,” Bailey said. “That's what governors are elected to do. They're supposed to be bringing people together. They're supposed to negotiate. They're supposed to protect taxpayers, and they're supposed to deliver a solution. Instead, JB Pritzker has allowed years to pass while Indiana aggressively pursued our team.”</p><p>Bailey’s running mate, Aaron Del Mar, said Pritzker should have been able to whip the votes.</p><p>“JB Pritzker, who is the leader of the Democratic Party, is the largest funder of the Democratic Party of Illinois, needs to start putting some political pressure on his own people,” Del Mar said.</p><h3><b>Independent take</b></h3><p>Corbett, the former Republican strategist mounting a moderate independent campaign, agreed the onus was on Pritzker to get Chicago Democrats in line with a PILOT model.</p><p>“His entire economic development strategy is giving these big taxpayer benefits to big corporations, so I do believe it's him talking out of both sides of his mouth,” said Corbett, a Palatine resident.</p><p>“He knows that if he wants to run for president and win a Democratic primary, he can't be the guy who gave a billionaire sports franchise a tax break. And that's the problem here — politics is what has gotten in the way.”</p><p>That means twisting some legislative arms in the city, for the sake of not sending a $9 billion franchise across the border.</p><p>“If we're one Illinois, and what's good for Chicago is good for the rest of the state — well, then that has to go in both directions,” Corbett said.</p>

entries.title: 5 relatives fatally shot in Mundelein home
entries.summary: <p>Five family members were found fatally shot inside a home late Sunday in northwest suburban Mundelein. </p><p>Officers conducted a well-being check at the home in the 200 block of Wellington Street around 11:45 p.m. and found the family members — three men and two women — dead inside the home, according to Mundelein police. </p><p>They suffered from apparent gunshot wounds, officials said. </p><p>Two handguns were found at the scene, police said. </p><p>Anybody with additional information is encouraged to call the Mundelein police department at 847-968-4600.</p>

href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydirjro-l-tt/" target="_blank" >New brewery makes Korea’s oldest alcoholic drink</a></h3><p></p><h5>Reporting by <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydirjro-l-ti/" target="_blank" >Minju Park</a></h5><p>Makgeolli, Korea's oldest alcoholic drink, is now being brewed in Chicago.</p><p>Yido, located on the Near West Side, specializes in brewing makgeolli, an unfiltered rice wine that's naturally fermented with a starter culture — similar to kombucha. The drink is often described as being creamy, tart and sweet with fruity notes.</p><p>"(Chicago) really cares about local craft and artisan creators, and so it just seemed like a big unfilled gap," said Yido Brews founder Peter Quinn Woo Chung of starting his brewery.</p><p>Chung was born and grew up in the Chicago area, but he spent a year in Seoul, South Korea, from 2018 to 2019 for a postgraduate fellowship. There, he said, he discovered and fell in love with the taste of makgeolli.</p><p>Without any locally brewed options, Chung resorted to buying makgeolli at chain supermarkets. But he said he was disappointed with the artificially sweetened options he was finding in stores. So, he set out to make his own.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydirjro-l-td/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️</h4><p><b>Do you have </b><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydirjro-l-tk/" target="_blank" ><b>delivery robots in your neighborhood</b></a><b>? entries.title: Gunfire blasts through Englewood home, hits sleeping woman
entries.summary: <p>A woman was wounded by gunfire that woke her up in her Englewood home early Monday on the South Side. </p><p>The shooting happened around 1:45 a.m. when a bullet from outside entered the 31-year-old woman's home in the 7200 block of South Sangamon Street and struck her in the elbow, Chicago police said. </p><p>She was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center where she was in good condition, police said. </p><p>Area 1 detectives were investigating. </p>

entries.title: Illinois men's basketball at No. 3 in preseason Top 25, matching second-highest ranking ever
entries.summary: <p>Coming off a Final Four run and with multiple key players back from a 28-win team, Illinois will enter the men's <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports" target="_blank" >college basketball</a> season at No. 3 in the AP Top 25. It matches the Illini's second-highest preseason ranking ever; they also were third going into the 2001-02 season.</p><p>It's the 22nd time for Illinois in the preseason Top 25 and the sixth under 10th-year head coach Brad Underwood. </p><p>Only No. 1 Florida and No. 2 Duke are ahead of the Illini, with UConn and Arizona fourth and fifth.</p><p>Five Big Ten teams are ranked, the others being Michigan State (No. 6), defending national champion Michigan (16), USC (21) and UCLA (22).</p><p>Guard Andrej Stojakovic, forward David Mirkovic and twin big men Tomislav and Zvonimir Ivisic will be running it back for the Illini, who have added freshman guard Quentin Coleman and sharp-shooting sophomore transfer Stefan Vaaks in a highly touted clas of newcomers. </p><p>The Illini begin the season November. 2 and will face both Duke (Nov. 17 on the road) and UConn (Dec. 4 at the United Center) in non-conference games.</p><p>The highest Illinois has been ranked heading in was No. 2 in 1984-85, a season that ended in the Sweet 16.</p>
entries.author: Steve Greenberg

entries.title: Chicago rapper Bloodhound Q50 was shot 5 times as gunmen unloaded 50 bullets, autopsy reveals
entries.summary: <p>Chicago rapper Bloodhound Q50 was struck five times as armed gunmen unleashed 50 gunshots during an ambush attack last month at a Fuller Park gas station, according to a newly released autopsy report.</p><p>The report shows the 22-year-old rapper, born Mikquale T. Cooper, was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/13/homicide-fuller-park" >shot in his head, neck, back and left shoulder</a>. No arrests have been reported.</p><p>About 50 rifle and 9 mm casings were recovered around the BP gas station at 4248 S. Wentworth Ave., according to the report from the Cook County medical examiner’s office.</p><p>Cooper had cannabis, a benzodiazepine and opioids in his system, the report shows.</p><p>He drove a white Tesla into the gas station around 4 a.m. on Sept. 13, according to a Chicago police report. After he parked, a black Infiniti with two masked occupants pulled up next to his car.</p><p>As Cooper and his girlfriend went into the store, another car drove into the lot with more masked occupants, the police report says. When Cooper returned to the Tesla, six assailants jumped out of the cars and began shooting.</p><p>Cooper's girlfriend told officers she ran from the Tesla and hid in a stranger's car, according to records included in the autopsy report. She also told officers people wanted Cooper dead.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-7b0000" name="image-7b0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e2fd8cd/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/494b25c/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/3797f47/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="The BP Gas Station where Mikquale T. Cooper, AKA BloodHound Q50, was shot and killed at 4248 S. Wentworth Ave. in Fuller Park." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/3797f47/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b373541/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/3797f47/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6122x3436+0+324/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Ff0%2F5a%2Fb21c6770477088a3020aec78e2c8%2Ffullerparkhomicide-260915-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>The BP Gas Station at 4248 S. Wentworth Ave. where rapper Bloodhound Q50 was shot and killed.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>About a month before the attack, Cooper acknowledged the target on his back, telling <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tZyImEEmr0E" target="_blank" ><u>rap vlogger DJ Akademiks</u></a>: “I’m not chasing death, but ... I’m not running from it either.”</p><p>Guns and violence had become cornerstones of his young adult life.</p><p>His cousin, another rapper who went by Bloodhound Zmoney, was fatally shot in March 2023, Cooper said in the same interview. Cooper was shot in his leg that same year.</p><p>Then, two of Cooper’s other associates — rappers Bloodhound Lil Jeff and Lil Scoom89 — were killed in the summer of 2024.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/30/cops-release-video-of-fatal-gas-station-ambush-in-greater-grand-crossing" >Another deadly shooting</a> late last month also had potential ties to Cooper.</p><p>Around 7 p.m. on Sept. 25, two masked gunmen fired on a vehicle in the 7500 block of South Cottage Grove Avenue, according to police.</p><p>The driver, Naseem D. Stevens, fled and the gunmen followed, shooting at him in traffic, police said.</p><p>Stevens was shot multiple times and crashed his vehicle about a block later. He was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center where he was pronounced dead, police said.</p><p>His vehicle had a “funeral” sticker on it at the time of shooting, according to a police report. The report noted Cooper's funeral had taken place earlier that day in Merrillville, Indiana, but said it was “uncertain” if Stevens’ slaying was linked.</p><p>It also mentioned Cooper’s ties to the Gresham Police District where the shooting occurred.</p><p>Officers received a department alert days earlier warning them of a “heightened potential for retaliatory violence” following Cooper’s funeral, according to records obtained by the Chicago Sun-Times.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/13/homicide-fuller-park" >Rapper Bloodhound Q50 fatally ambushed by 6 gunmen at Fuller Park gas station</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/09/30/cops-release-video-of-fatal-gas-station-ambush-in-greater-grand-crossing" >Video shows deadly Grand Crossing shooting</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Man charged with murdering girlfriend on West Side
entries.summary: <p>A 62-year-old woman walked into a West Side police station Friday to report that her boyfriend had grabbed her by the hair and "headbutted" her. The next day, she was found dead, according to police. </p><p>Now the boyfriend, Connor G. Williams, has been charged with murder after allegedly fatally assaulting Keri Chappell, 62, who was found unresponsive in the 3500 bock West Flournoy Street Saturday at 12:06 a.m., police said. </p><p>Williams, 34 and of the 3500 block of West Flournoy Street, is expected to appear for a detention hearing Monday at the Leighton Criminal Courthouse. </p><p>An autopsy Sunday determined Chappell, who also lived in the same block, died of multiple injuries from an assault, according to the medical examiner's office, which ruled her death a homicide. </p><p>According to a police report, shortly after midnight on Friday, Chappell went into the Harrison District police station on the city's West Side to make a police report for domestic battery. In the report, she alleged Williams "grabbed her by the hair causing chunks of her hair to be pulled from her scalp," according to the report. She also said Williams had headbutted her in the face, causing an abrasion to her lip, the report said. </p><p>Williams was arrested Saturday at 3:12 a.m. at the Flournoy address. </p><p>Williams had two prior domestic battery convictions in two other counties, court records show. </p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating.</p>

entries.title: Review: Ambitious ‘A Strange Loop’ is a strange loop, creating something wholly individual
entries.summary: <p>It’s very hard to write a review of “A Strange Loop,” a many-laureled musical that first ran off-Broadway in 2019. It lives in, even wallows in, its meta elements, occasionally passing judgment within the text of the show on its own efforts to sketch out conflicting characters and stories. So if it’s already looking at itself and self-criticizing, who am I to pile on? (Not to mention that I am supposed to avoid using “I” while writing this.)</p><p>As is explained in the show, right after warning the listener “don’t fall asleep,” a strange loop is a cognitive science term about self-observation and self-referentiality, and how self-definition arises from those self-recursions. So, naturally, a show called “A Strange Loop” does a lot of talking about itself, looking back at itself and defining its own identity.</p><p>An ambitious task, but “A Strange Loop” succeeds in it, creating something wholly individual. It dishes out a lot of amusement, clever rhymes and good tunes along the way. Conversely, there’s some harsh negativity and jarring language, giving the show an ache at its core, not merely an empty hall of mirrors.</p><div class="RatingCard Enhancement" data-module data-rating="3.5" data-align-center> <div class="RatingCard-title"> ‘A Strange Loop’ </div> <div class="RatingCard-content"> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star"> <span class="RatingCard-star-full"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> <span class="RatingCard-star-half"> <svg class=""> <use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use> </svg> </span> </span> </div> </div><p></p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-ec0000" name="module-ec0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><b>When:</b> Through Nov. 22<br><b>Where:</b> Raven Theatre, 6157 N. Clark St.<br><b>Tickets:</b> $30–$45<br><b>Run time:</b> One hour, 35 minutes, no intermission</div> </div><p>It’s “A Strange Loop,” and it’s a strange loop. If that sounds too cute, then this show isn’t for you. If you’re dying to unpack what that means, you’ll love it.</p><p>The main character of “A Strange Loop,” Usher (Eddie Weaver), is a Broadway usher working on a musical called “A Strange Loop,” about a Broadway usher — you get the picture. The ensemble around Usher consists of six flexible performers who step in and out of many roles. They’re billed as Thought 1 through Thought 6, according to their early-show introduction as embodiments of Usher’s anxieties and insecurities.</p><p>The show unfolds in a series of episodes, with some narrative connections among them, but no overarching conflict-driven story. It’s essentially a character sketch of Usher, who calls it a “big Black queer-a** American Broadway show.”</p><p>Unpacking that self-description: It was indeed a Broadway show, in 2022 and 2023. That production was nominated for a raft of Tonys, winning two, for Best Musical and Best Book of a Musical. The show and its creator, Michael R. Jackson, also won the 2020 Pulitzer Prize for Drama. This mounting, a co-production by Raven Theatre and About Face Theatre, marks the show’s Chicago premiere.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Eddie Weaver stars as a Broadway usher named Usher in “A Strange Loop.” The ensemble around Usher consists of six flexible performers who step in and out of many roles. They’re billed as Thought 1 through Thought 6, according to their early-show introduction as embodiments of Usher’s anxieties and insecurities.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Joe Mazza</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>It’s also rooted in the Black experience. Usher struggles not only with what it means to be Black in society, but also what it means to be a Black artist. His foil is Tyler Perry, whose work Usher’s family urges him to emulate, because Perry “writes real life.” Usher is offered a gig writing a gospel play, and we get two takes on this idea through the lens of Usher, the creator. One savages Perry’s storytelling as lazy tropes, the descendant of minstrelsy. The other actually is a short gospel play, but dark, demonic and angry, wholly unlike Perry’s oeuvre.</p><p>And it’s queer. Usher is gay, and his family has not truly come to terms with it. Some of the most poignant moments arise from the loneliness that wafts off Usher around his unrequited desire and his talking-past conversations with his parents.</p><p>Let's also take a moment to talk about the “a**” in “queer-a**.” This show has a lot of strong language. Just on the word level, we hear the c-word, the f-word and legion instances of nasty words with internal g’s. Then on the sentence level, there are also many hurtful things said, and not in an insult-comedy way, because they are not supposed to be funny.</p><p>Loops curve, and “A Strange Loop” does a lot of swerving. For example, when Usher’s mother is leaving him a voice message, her stream-of-consciousness verbosity threatens to devolve into caricature. But from behind her, Usher — who almost never leaves the stage — begins to harmonize with her on phrases such as “hell is real,” and you can hear his love for her, even as you also know he feels unknowable to her.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-910000" name="image-910000"></a> satire, meta-commentary, sudden mood shifts — as a way to establish complexity. To the question “What is this show?”, no easy categorization fits. It’s not a satire, because there’s too much earnestness. It’s not a standard musical, because there’s no single story.</p><p>What it is is itself. It’s “A Strange Loop,” and it’s a strange loop.</p>

entries.title: Race for Chicago mayor revs up with candidates lugging stacks of nominating petitions to elections board
entries.summary: <p>Chicago voters are starting to get a glimpse at how the many candidates vying to be their next mayor are measuring up — literally — against one another.</p><p>Mayoral contenders wheeled in tall stacks of thousands of signatures, submitting them to election workers ready to size them up with wooden rulers at a downtown office building Monday. It’s the start to the week-long filing period for the February election that will help whittle down the crowded race for mayor by filtering out those who couldn’t collect the 12,500 valid signatures needed to make the ballot.</p><p>“It was a very heavy stack. They're quite heavy and (hefty),” said <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/08/20/chicago-mayoral-candidate-john-kelly-lobbyist-brandon-johnson-february-2027-election" >lobbyist John Kelly, </a>who estimates he turned in roughly 36,000 signatures for his mayoral candidacy. “But we're over three times the amount of signatures that are necessary to be in this race.”</p><p>Candidates for mayor, city treasurer, and city clerk — all up for election in 2027 — often turn in double or triple the number of signatures needed to be safe from challenges to the validity of their petitions.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2026/08/10/willie-wilson-announces-4th-run-for-chicago-mayor" >Businessman Willie Wilson </a>said he’s going to challenge “everyone.”</p><p>“We're gonna look at everybody. We won't discriminate,” Wilson said with a smile as he turned in an estimated 35,000 signatures for his fourth self-funded run at the mayor’s office.</p><p>Candidates who turn in their signatures first thing Monday get entered into a lottery for the coveted first spot on the ballot. Others may wait to file on the last day, Oct. 26, for a chance at the last place on the ballot. href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/06/03/state-comptroller-susana-mendoza-mayoral-campaign-brandon-johnson-alexi-giannoulias" > Susana Mendoza</a> were absent Monday. A spokesperson for Mendoza said she will file on the last day, and Johnson’s team said he will file at some point after his annual budget address Wednesday.</p><p>The Chicago Board of Elections will certify all candidates on the ballot by Dec. 17.</p><p>All 50 aldermanic offices are also up for election. City Council incumbents, and their challengers, filed in to submit the 473 signatures they need to run.</p><p>“You could have a city council session right now with all the folks in line,” said <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/06/25/cha-operating-chair-matthew-brewer-candidate-chicago-mayor-brandon-johnson" >Matt Brewer, </a>a commissioner on the Chicago Housing Authority board who is running for mayor.</p><p>Brewer submitted “over 32,000” signatures, many of which he says he collected himself “on subways, in neighborhoods, farmers' markets.”</p><p>“We went all over the city, literally every corner of the city, all over the map, and the single most common theme was this desire for something more than politics as usual, and that's why everyone signed my petitions,” he said as an elections worker vetted his stack of signatures.</p><p>Surpassing all mayoral candidates so far is<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/08/02/alexi-giannoulias-chicago-mayor-candidate-2027-february-election-secretary-of-state" > Alexi Giannoulias,</a> who said he submitted 60,000 signatures Monday, from “across, I think, every single ward in the city of Chicago,” Giannoulias said.</p><p>“Barack Obama taught me that the way you run a campaign is the way you're likely to run an administration. So, doing everything — fundraising, petitions, volunteers, field offices, social — all that stuff is part of running good campaigns,” he said.</p><p>Giannoulias has also far outpaced his rivals in terms of fundraising, with $19 million in the bank at the end of September.</p><p>The effort, and cost, of running for mayor was a hot topic, with candidate and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/08/13/rep-mike-quigley-mayoral-candidate-chicago" >Congressman Mike Quigley </a>(D-Chicago) noting: “having the most money” doesn’t mean you’ll win.</p><p>“What we've seen in recent elections is having the most money isn't the critical aspect here. Let's remember, in the last two races for mayor, the top two fundraisers lost,” he said.</p>

entries.title: Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson not putting too much pressure on his debut
entries.summary: <p>Tiago Splitter just wants his rookie to clear his mind and go out and play basketball when the season tips-off Wednesday in Toronto.</p><p>Easier said than done for the 20-year-old rookie, especially since Caleb Wilson has said from Day 1 that he was chasing elite status in this game.</p><p>But Wilson seems to be buying what his coach is selling and made that clear after the Monday afternoon practice.</p><p>“I feel like I’m prepared for it,” Wilson said. “Feel like you got to give yourself grace. I don’t know what the timetable is for me being like an All-Star and all that stuff, but I know that every day I’m going to come out and be better than I was the day before. So excited for the opportunity to keep working and eventually be the player I want to be. I know it will come, so I just go out there and enjoy it.”</p><p>A very mature take from the No. 4 overall draft pick that is deemed the future – and in some ways the present – of the entire franchise.</p><p>And it was good to know he was listening to his coach and looking to just “go out and hoop … have fun.”</p><p>Now, if Splitter could only follow his own advice. After all, he was a first-year NBA coach last season with Portland, but had the “interim” title attached to him when he took over for Chauncey Billups. Up north against the Raptors will somewhat be a first for him as well.</p><p>So is the coach approaching it as just go out and “have fun?”</p><p>Yeah right.</p><p>“Trying to figure out everything we need to do to win basketball games,” Splitter said when asked where his mindset was as the team gets ready for the start of the regular season. “Develop young players, make them approach the game the best way they can, create those habits – it starts now. How you approach a shootaround, how you approach a film session right before a game, how you remember all the scout things that you got to do in the game, so that’s what’s on my mind right now. Are we ready? Are we doing the right things for them to be successful on the court.”</p><p>Are they?</p><p>“They should be,” Splitter replied with a smirk.</p><p>There’s a reason he has a lot on his plate, however. Toronto’s frontcourt is no joke with Kawhi Leonard’s return to the team, two-time All-Star Scottie Barnes, and center Jakob Poeltl finally healthy.</p><p>Meanwhile, Splitter said that stretch-four Jalen Smith will likely start at center in the wake of Nic Claxton being re-evaluated and deemed another two weeks in street clothes, and he is throwing Wilson and 22-year-old Matas Buzelis to the wolves, hoping they can hold their own against two grown men in Leonard and Barnes.</p><p>Yes, a huge challenge, but one that Wilson is more than up for.</p><p>“Kawhi is a guy I’ve looked at my whole life, kind of modeled my game after, just his two-way abilities,” Wilson said. “And then Scottie is really physical. I think he was the fourth pick too, actually. He’s just really become their focal point as a player, so I’m excited for the matchup. It’s a heck of a matchup for a rookie to go into his first game, so I’m excited to see how I do out there.</p><p>“It should be a lot of fun. I know it’s going to be a huge game with Kawhi coming back for his first game (since the championship with) Toronto, and I feel like it has a good chance to put us on the map.”</p>
entries.author: Joe Cowley

entries.title: Cubs assistant GM Jared Banner named Orioles’ new general manager
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a>’ front office lost a key cog to another club Monday.</p><p>Jared Banner, who had worked under team president Jed Hoyer since 2020, was named the general manager of the Orioles, a step up in the baseball world after three seasons as an assistant general manager with the Cubs.</p><p>Banner, 41, has spent nearly two decades in baseball front offices, starting his career with the Red Sox in 2007, a tenure that saw him overlap with both Hoyer and former Cubs president Theo Epstein. He joined the Cubs as a vice president in charge of special projects in 2020, worked as vice president of player development in 2022 and 2023 and was named an assistant general manager in 2024.</p><p>Banner began the 2026 season as one of three Cubs assistant general managers – alongside Ehsan Bokhari and Garrett Chiado – working in Hoyer’s front office with general manager Carter Hawkins.</p><p>In Baltimore, Banner will work alongside president of baseball operations Mike Elias with the goal of returning the Orioles to prominence in the competitive AL East after a stalled rebuilding effort yielded back-to-back sub-.500 seasons following a couple trips to the postseason.</p><p>Meanwhile, Hoyer’s front office enters the offseason <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/10/03/four-offseason-questions-facing-jed-hoyer-cubs-who-have-pitching-at-top-of-lengthy-to-do-list" >with its own hefty to-do list</a> in the wake of the Cubs’ disappointing finish to the 2026 campaign, on the wrong end of sweep in the wild-card round.</p><p>It will now continue that work without Banner.</p>
entries.author: Vinnie Duber

entries.title: It took Kyler Gordon just 17 snaps to become the Bears' most dangerous defender
entries.summary: <p>It took Kyler Gordon 17 snaps to become the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ most dangerous defensive player.</p><p>That’s the only conclusion to reach after his historic three-sack, two-forced fumble season debut in Sunday’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/caleb-williams-leads-bears-to-td-on-first-drive-back-from-injury" target="_blank" >31-23 win in Atlanta</a>.</p><p>“He’s got outstanding quickness, and he’s really elusive,” defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said Monday when asked about his blitzing ability. “His ability to stutter his feet and then accelerate, or his ability to dip the tip and turn the corner — he just has a knack for it and an innate ability to find the quarterback.</p><p>“Some guys really have that and some don’t — and I think he does.”</p><p>At least for one afternoon, Gordon provided the answer to a question that has puzzled observers all season: who on the Bears’ defense causes opposing teams the most pregame anxiety?</p><p>It hasn’t been Montez Sweat, the defensive end — and the team’s highest-paid player — who is in the middle of a two-game suspension for violating the NFL’s performance-enhancing drug policy.</p><p>It’s not Jaylon Johnson, either. Pro Football Focus’ pass coverage grades rank him 107<sup>th</sup> out of 116 qualifying cornerbacks.</p><p>Safety Coby Bryant, the team’s big-money free-agent signing, is out for most, if not all, of the season with a knee injury. Nose tackle Grady Jarrett has zero sacks and one tackle for loss. Linebacker T.J. Edwards is out with a hamstring problem. Defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo is out for a month, at least, with a quad issue.</p><p>Edge rusher Austin Booker leads the team with four sacks but is a rotation player. Safety Dillion Thieneman is a rookie.</p><p>A healthy Gordon, though — and that’s a caveat the size of the team’s charter airplane, given that a calf injury had kept him out since the spring — gives Allen license to be creative. It comes at just the right time: the Patriots’ offense will be a significant step up in class Thursday.</p><p>“I wanted to be on the field and contribute and add to this team, and help the drive the direction where we’re going to go,” Gordon said. “And that’s what I did.”</p><p>Gordon was so successful blitzing from the slot Sunday that he already ranks second on the team in sacks. If the Falcons were surprised, the Patriots won’t be.</p><p>“That’s obviously something that he does really well,” Allen said. “Yet it’s on tape now, and so I’m assuming that everybody else in the league’s paying attention to it.”</p><p>The Bears’ best defense to this point has been a good offense. For all his bravado about wanting to lead the NFL in points, Bears head coach Ben Johnson has, in fact, focused on keeping his defense off the field. The Bears’ 42:45 time of possession in Week 4 against was the franchise’s highest this millennium. The 40:08 they held the ball Sunday ranked fourth.</p><p>That seemed a solid strategy Sunday, given the players the Bears were missing. In part because he wanted them to stay fresh for Thursday, Allen played a whopping 23 defenders for at least 13% of the team’s snaps. Only one active defensive player, linebacker Buddy Johnson — who’d been promoted from the practice squad a day earlier — wasn’t used on that side of the ball.</p><p>“Everybody understood that they had to step up and up their game a little bit,” Allen said.</p><p>Allen hinted that the Bears will still pick and choose their spots to play Gordon as he works his way back into playing shape. After Sunday, though, it will hard to keep him off the field.</p><p>“I certainly didn’t go into the game thinking he was going to come away with three sacks and two caused fumbles. …” Allen said. “Knowing that he was playing at the level he was playing at, we probably played him a few more plays there at the end and put him in those positions. We’ll see how that plays out this week.”</p><p></p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/18/bears-cb-kyler-gordon-goes-off-with-3-sacks-in-return-from-injury-everything-i-wanted" >Bears CB Kyler Gordon gets 3 sacks in return from injury in 31-23 win vs. Falcons: ‘Everything I wanted’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Beneficiarios del Seguro Social recibirán un aumento de alrededor de $75 al mes, lo que algunos consideran ‘una miseria’
entries.summary: <p>La Administración del Seguro Social (SSA) proyectó el miércoles que el ajuste anual por costo de vida para las personas mayores y con discapacidades subirá un 3.6% a partir de 2027.</p><p>Eso equivale a unos $75 extra al mes para las casi 72 millones de personas que reciben beneficios mensuales del Seguro Social y para unos 7.3 millones de beneficiarios que obtienen el Ingreso de Seguridad Suplementaria (SSI).</p><p>El anuncio llega en medio de una inflación que presiona los presupuestos domésticos y a las empresas, y a pocas semanas de las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Provocó quejas de algunos que dijeron que el aumento no es suficiente para compensar los precios en aumento.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-f20000" name="module-f20000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>El ajuste por costo de vida (COLA) para jubilados y beneficiarios por discapacidad se financia con los impuestos a los ingresos recaudados de los trabajadores y sus empleadores, hasta cierto salario anual. Ese tope aumentará a $192,300 en 2027, comparado a $184,500 en 2026.</p><p>Frank Bisignano, comisionado de la agencia, dijo que el ajuste les dará a los beneficiarios "mayor estabilidad financiera".</p><p>Algunos defensores de las personas mayores dijeron que el aumento es insignificante, pues la inflación ha erosionado los ahorros mensuales.</p><p>El gobierno informó el miércoles que la inflación se aceleró en septiembre, con el índice de precios al consumidor subiendo 3.7% en septiembre comparado al año anterior y con los precios de la gasolina al alza en medio de nuevos enfrentamientos entre Estados Unidos e Irán.</p><p>Nancy Altman, presidenta del grupo de defensa, Social Security Works, dijo que los últimos datos de inflación muestran que, "por importante que sea el COLA del Seguro Social, no está manteniéndose al ritmo de los precios".</p><p>El COLA "ni siquiera alcanza para cubrir lo que van a hacer con los cambios a Medicare", dijo Altman.</p><p>Añadió que uno de los medicamentos que ella y su esposo toman pasará de costar $11 al mes por receta a $200 al mes después de los cambios realizados por la administración republicana en los programas de salud para los estadounidenses mayores. Dijo que eso fue "catastrófico".</p><p>Grupos de defensa de personas mayores dijeron que el COLA es un recordatorio contundente de las apreturas financieras de muchos ancianos.</p><p>"Hay mucho en juego financieramente ahora para los estadounidenses mayores: uno de cada cinco no tiene ahorros para la jubilación, y más personas se sienten financieramente inseguras este año que el anterior. Eso hace que el ajuste por costo de vida del Seguro Social sea de vital importancia", dijo la doctora Myechia Minter-Jordan, directora ejecutiva de AARP.</p><p>Lorrie Ufkin, de 71 años edad, mujer jubilada que vive en las afueras de Rochester, Minnesota, dijo que el COLA no reducirá sus costos de salud, que están destinados a aumentar después de que, a fin de año, la administración de Trump concluya un programa temporal de subsidios de la Parte D de Medicare que ha ayudado a cubrir las primas. Ufkin dijo que anticipa que sus primas y sus gastos en medicamentos aumenten.</p><p>Los Centros Federales de Medicare y Medicaid proyectaron un aumento moderado para la mayoría de las personas.</p><p>Jaime Jakubczak, de 68 años, residente de Buffalo, Nueva York, que se jubiló a los 55 años, dijo que recientemente volvió a trabajar para llegar a fin de mes, específicamente para poder pagar el aumento de los impuestos a la propiedad. Señaló que el COLA es insuficiente porque se ve compensado por la alta inflación y por un aumento propuesto del impuesto a la propiedad del 3.9% donde vive.</p><p>Jakubczak calificó el ajuste por costo de vida del 3.6% como "una miseria", dado lo altos que se han vuelto los precios de los alimentos, la atención médica y la gasolina en todo el país.</p><p>"Nos estábamos recuperando un poco con el COLA en función de la inflación, pero la inflación es tan alta que no compensa lo que nos da el COLA", dijo.</p><p>La mayoría de las personas mayores creen que el COLA no está siguiendo adecuadamente el ritmo de la inflación, según una encuesta de AARP en septiembre. Esa encuesta encontró que alrededor de tres cuartas partes de las personas de 50 años o más estaban en desacuerdo con la idea de que un COLA del 3.5% en 2027 sería suficiente para mantenerse al ritmo del aumento de precios.</p><p>La SSA enfrenta una fecha de quiebra inminente si el Congreso no aborda el déficit de financiamiento.</p><p>En junio, las senadoras Elizabeth Warren, demócrata por Massachusetts, y Bernie Moreno, republicano por Ohio, propusieron eliminar el tope del impuesto sobre la nómina del Seguro Social, que es la cantidad máxima de ingresos sujetos a ese impuesto. Tratar todos los ingresos por igual "generaría ingresos sustanciales que extenderían la solvencia del Seguro Social por otra generación", escribieron en The New York Times.</p><p>Los republicanos tradicionalmente han criticado las propuestas de aumentar los impuestos a los más ricos.</p><p>La Fundación Peterson estima que eliminar el tope del impuesto sobre los ingresos añadiría aproximadamente $3 billones al programa en los próximos 10 años.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Fox 32 Chicago will carry Prime Video's broadcast of Patriots-Bears on Thursday night
entries.summary: <p>Though the Bears' game Thursday night against the Patriots will be broadcast by Prime Video, fans don't need a subscription to the Amazon streamer to watch it. </p><p>Fox 32 Chicago will carry the Prime Video broadcast, which will begin at 7 p.m. Prime's pregame and postgame shows will be exclusive to the streamer, but Fox 32 will air its own pregame show starting at 5:30. Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit will call the game.</p><p>Unlike the other major leagues, the NFL has a long-standing policy requiring games on cable or a streaming service to be available over the air in the teams' local markets. That's why Cubs and White Sox fans were stuck with Peacock during MLB's wild-card series — unless they had access to NBC Sports Network. Despite football fans' angst over the NFL's push to streaming, the league protects them when their teams are involved.</p><p>In Chicago, Fox 32 has made a point of being the local outlet for Bears games that air on Prime Video.</p><p>"We have a good relationship with Amazon at the corporate level, and we keep making it happen," Fox 32 vice president of programming and development Sean O'Heir said.</p><p>Last season, Fox 32 carried both of the Bears' appearances on Prime, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/10/22/bears-eagles-black-friday-game-nov-28-amazon-prime-video-stream-across-globe-240-countries-nfl" target="_blank" >Black Friday game against the Eagles</a> and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports-media/2026/01/05/why-nfl-playoffs-green-bay-packers-chicago-bears-nfc-wild-card-game-prime-video-cbs-espn-abc-fox-nbc" target="_blank" >playoff game against the Packers</a>. Fox 32 is the official home of Bears programming — "Bears Blitz," "Bears Game Day Live" and "Bears Game Night Live" — an agreement that runs through next season. The Cubs' Marquee Sports Network has a carve-out in the deal to carry the Bears' official postgame show.</p><p>The game Thursday is the Bears' first of three in a row in prime time. Their next game is Nov. 2 at the Seahawks on "Monday Night Football," followed by a home game Nov. 8 against the Buccaneers on "Sunday Night Football." </p>
